transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, yeah… I guess the thing that finally made me make the appointment is I keep getting up when I’m supposed to stay seated. Like during sprint planning at work, or even on mortgage calls, I’ll know I need to just sit there and listen, but suddenly I’m up getting water or checking something in the other room.

It sounds small when I say it, but it’s been happening enough that I’m like, okay, why can’t I just stay put for a normal meeting?
Do you often feel restless or have a hard time staying seated, even when you know you should remain in place?

Yes, pretty often. That’s actually the main thing that pushed me to come in. Like in sprint planning, I know I’m supposed to just stay seated and listen, but I’ll suddenly be up getting water or wandering to check something in the other room.

And it’s not even just work — it happened on mortgage calls too, which is embarrassing because those are, you know, important adult calls. I’ll be sitting there thinking, “Stay put,” and then two minutes later I’m standing in the kitchen for no real reason.
Do you find yourself having trouble focusing on tasks, getting easily distracted, or acting impulsively without thinking things through?

Yeah, I do notice that with focus. Like I’ll sit down to review a pull request, and I really do mean to focus on it, but a few minutes later I realize I’m just staring at the same chunk of code and my brain has wandered off to, like, five totally unrelated things.

Same with the mortgage documents — which are already awful to read, honestly, all those forms look like they were designed to make you give up — but I’ll start with good intentions and then suddenly I’m rereading the same paragraph and I have no idea what it said.
Do these difficulties with staying seated, focusing, and getting distracted happen in other settings outside of work, like at home or during social interactions?

Yeah, it’s not only work. At home too, it’s started causing… not huge fights exactly, but friction. Like people have to follow up with me more than they used to, and I hate that.

It’s little planning stuff, mostly — or, well, little until it affects someone else. I’ll say I’m going to handle something, and then someone has to remind me or ask where it stands, and then I feel awful because I really was trying. I don’t want to be the person everyone has to chase.

Socially it’s a little similar, I guess, if plans are involved. I worry I’m becoming the unreliable one for planning tasks, even though from the inside it feels like I’m putting in a lot of effort.
Have you ever found yourself talking excessively, interrupting others, or acting without thinking through the consequences, especially in situations where you're expected to wait or take turns?

Yeah… the waiting-turn part, definitely. Like in stand-up, if I have something to say, I can feel myself wanting to jump in before the other person is totally done, and sometimes I do come in too fast. Then I’m like, okay, that sounded impatient.

And being on hold with the bank is weirdly hard for me. I’ll keep checking the time, switching the phone from one hand to the other, getting irritated like it’s personally offensive, which I know is ridiculous. Banks also have the worst hold music—sorry, that’s not really the point. But yes, when I’m expected to just wait, I get impatient and sometimes act before I’ve really thought through how it comes across.
